answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a per-identity bond escrowed before an agent can vote or claim rewards. Each new agent must post a stake sized to exceed the expected value of a rewarded epoch, so a farmer spinning up many identities must fund every one up front. Because the bond is locked and slashed on proof of collusion, each fake agent is a credible sunk cost, not a free alias. The mechanism acts as a lantern on cheap clones: only agents holding real capital beside an island of honest peers pass the terrace of entry, and cloning multiplies the attacker's exposure instead of dividing it.
